resolved_during_review.title: Uncertainty recording must not overwrite a structural recovery cause
resolved_during_review.before: record_uncertain unconditionally replaced the durable journal-loss reason with UNKNOWN_REASON. Existing object remained blocked only by its cached structural cause; a reopened object with recreated consistent checkpoints could then quarantine the gap and report ready.
resolved_during_review.original_probe: Real record_uncertain plus real _transaction and generation_readiness on a SQL-behavior memory stub reproduced durable downgrade and fresh ready=true. No SQLite, processes, files or original ledger were used.
resolved_during_review.fix: Core owner added shared _record_recovery_reason preserving the first structural cause, with UNKNOWN promotion only to structural; all recovery cause writers use it. _current_recovery_reason lets newer durable structural cause override cached UNKNOWN. No unchanged identity row replacement.
resolved_during_review.recheck: Seven pure logical transition probes match expected preserved structural/readiness=false and sticky/cached precedence behavior. Tests for missing journal then uncertainty/reopen and cached UNKNOWN/new durable structural cause were source-reviewed but not executed by this reviewer.

semantic_review.conclusion: Quarantine builds a separate immutable descriptor, retaining the original raw producer session hash, whole original run, uncertain floor, reservation, retry ordinal and unsettled intent. Current output hashes are present-day evidence; no lost gross history or original observation is reconstructed.

Application requires the designated coordinator, intact original ledger/checkpoints, inactive exact recorded native owners/groups, absent registered resources, stable output identity/inventory, and a hash-bound external assertion. The external assertion is explicitly operator-attested; engine does not authenticate its truth or host authority.

Local descriptor SQL/checkpoint transaction precedes catalog publication. A failed publication leaves full local holds and blocks manager generation on local/published mismatch; retry reuses the immutable descriptor. Checkpoint-before-commit failure and revision/inventory mismatch remain blockers.

Portable/checkpoint descriptors preserve floors, holds and original failure metadata without creating original producer sessions or authoritative generation readiness. Missing database/journal and reconstructed catalog history retain structural causes across uncertainty recording and reopen.

Admission preserves unchanged cumulative numeric limits, known original charges, whole pending reservations and retry count; quarantined runs and output roots cannot be reused or settled/reconciled into success. These lower-bound sums do not establish a physical maximum for missing history.

Healthy distinct target intents may settle while verified historical quarantines remain unsettled. Catalog replay binds reservation/run/unit/intent/reserved amounts and rejects settlement or changed/replayed quarantine bindings. Scoped final receipt readiness requires only quarantined pending intents, exact quarantined pending counts and no other outstanding run rows.

Producer saves final stable observation before settlement and retains it when later accounting fails. Final hash/inventory/root identity failures are separately explicit even after earlier aggregate failure. Oversized proof is rejected with compact incomplete failure marker, raw files preserved and full reservation retained.

No quarantine operation marks original failure complete, grants product acceptance, changes QA/DoD duties, or authorizes implementation. Initial unknown records with no original hashes stay historically incomplete.
